Legacy grpc.ts uses separate fileContainingSymbol calls/roots per listed service; descriptor-client dependency cache is shared and concurrent arrival timing remains an explicit separate boundary. Then expand dependency/extras/service-list/order controls, saved real multi-service scenarios, fresh audited build/full regression/independent closure and topic commit. ## gRPC reconnect socket candidate scheduling — 2026-10-19

Source parent f3383d88. Selected Tonic channels previously retried disconnected static/resolved destinations serially inside their connector: a pending first TCP/CONNECT attempt could consume the entire connection timeout without trying remaining candidates. grpc_proxy.rs now races those reconnect sockets/complete CONNECT tunnels with the existing250ms Happy Eyeballs interval, advances immediately only when the latest-started candidate fails, and retains an absolute timer across older failures. Initial full Tonic handshake racing remains one socket per candidate; reconnect starts from that connector's own cursor, refreshes/interleaves DNS as before, and advances its cursor after the selected socket. No spawned tasks: returning, error or cancellation drops all losing futures/transports. Endpoint still owns timeout/TLS/HTTP2; reconnect racing here selects TCP/CONNECT completion, not full TLS/HTTP2 completion, so that broader compatibility gate remains explicit.

## Owned pool-driven DNS/TXT re-resolution — 2026-10-19

Source parent4d25a18c. Active RR pool health transitions now publish re-resolution requests when an observed parent had Ready children and a child transitions away from Ready, including another child's non-Ready transition while the parent is Ready. Shared health map serializes that decision; initial unchanged Connecting reports do not trigger requests. Generation-aware reporting infers a lost old connection when watch coalesces directly from Ready to a new Ready generation, so fast reconnect does not suppress the request.

Added grpc_lb_resolution.rs event-driven worker owned by the dynamic route owner. It subscribes to the current RR route's request stream, switches subscriptions on route epochs and retains the receiver through each lookup rather than replaying historical requests in a loop. A loss predating the initial subscription remains pending once. Requests during cooldown coalesce into one deferred lookup, and requests during an active lookup coalesce/are consumed after it. No periodic polling or DNS call while a healthy unchanged route is idle. The worker invokes the existing resolver, whose fresh successful canonical publication already updates policy/address revisions.

DNS records the latest lookup attempt start per target generation, including attempts that fail, and the worker waits until that start+30seconds before executing a requested update rather than returning a fresh cached result and silently losing the request. Within each logical DNS resolver, callbacks waiting on an in-flight address lookup now consume the completed result, including its error, instead of each waiter issuing another lookup after a failure. A completion epoch is sampled before acquiring the existing lookup mutex; completion and cached result are published under that mutex. ## DNS failure backoff scheduling (2026-10-19)

The shared per-resolver lookup cache now owns default backoff timing: 1000ms initial, 1.6 multiplier, 120000ms cap before +/-20 percent jitter, fractional milliseconds truncated. The clock begins at attempt start so a slow failure spends its own delay; success clears/reset backoff. A later independent connector/worker request waits only the remaining failure backoff. Overlapping callbacks still share the same completed answer/error. DNS failure replaces the successful 30-second minimum deadline with the failed attempt backoff deadline and retains previously published LB addresses. No unconditional failure polling/retry loop is introduced: another LB/connector request is required.

Resolution timing has its own watch signal, separate from policy/address revisions. The RR worker re-evaluates a deferred deadline when another lookup changes timing, including clearing the minimum timer on error; this does not cancel a pending policy build. Failure publication checks both target generation and exact latest attempt start. Target retirement remains handled by the existing owned-worker cancellation. ## Pending native RR re-resolution authority (2026-10-19)

The policy owner now publishes an explicit latest-child request subscription independently of the route used by RPCs. A pending RR pool starts and supplies its subscription before awaiting its first non-Connecting state; the old RR pool's source is revoked during replacement even while its route continues serving. A pending buffered policy publishes no RR source. Successful promotion preserves the same pending pool subscription, avoiding replay on route installation. If a superseded build returns to the current route, the current pool is re-subscribed with requests emitted while unauthorized discarded. Initial route history is retained once.

The resolver worker follows source changes with priority over old-pool signals and retains each subscription through its lookup. Already accepted DNS requests finish through cooldown/lookup unless target retirement cancels them; child source changes alone do not cancel accepted resolver work. A closed retired request stream waits for replacement publication instead of spinning. Source watches hold only receivers, not pool/Entry/route owners. Pending pool cancellation and Owner Drop keep the existing owned abort paths. ## Native pick_first DNS routing and membership (2026-10-19)

Unproxied named DNS targets now use native PickFirst over exact-reservation singleton subchannels instead of the buffered connect_resolved adapter. Its owned worker interleaves address families after policy shuffle, starts candidates at 250ms intervals, advances the latest candidate early on observed connection failure, selects an observed READY subchannel, drops competing candidate owners and retains the exact selected Entry through response bodies. A READY selected address still in the list is reused before opening new connections; pending subchannels with matching addresses are reused on list updates. Pending PickFirst and RR publish their own request subscriptions before first-state decisions; latest-child authority now includes native PickFirst, and removed buffered DNS reconnect callbacks no longer bypass it. ## Preserve selected unary status across cancellation during payload ACK (2026-10-19)

Final unary response delivery now carries its already selected status as internal context. Event::FinalMessage serializes exactly as the existing kind message/text payload; its boxed status is serde-skipped and never reaches renderer JSON. Native Delivery remembers that status before queuing the final payload and clears it when the status packet is sent. If Cancel arrives while the payload ACK is pending (or just completed), the stopped call future releases resources and Delivery resumes the original payload ACK with its original deadline, then sends the chosen status instead of overwriting final OK with CANCELLED. Existing terminal packet protection remains. Active server/bidirectional messages have no final context and retain normal cancellation behavior.

Contract pinned grpc-js1.14.4 client.ts final OK selects the unary callback/data result before the legacy forwarded status event; cancellation after that selection must not replace it. No renderer/API packet shape/layout change, dependency/vendor change or new background task. ## Nested child policy replacement ownership (2026-10-19)

Continues cf186a8b. Pool policy config now retains the complete selected kind path (each outlier wrapper and RR/weighted leaf). Dynamic route current/pending identity compares this path instead of only root Kind, so same-outer-kind nested/leaf changes construct a separate pending pool, retain the current route while pending Connecting, and publish on the existing non-Connecting decision/revision guard. A newer different path supersedes the pending route; same-path updates revise that pending owner. Resolver requests continue to follow only the latest pending/current source. No policy instance is now changed in place merely because its root kind stayed outlier_detection.

Outlier layers now use Arc<Mutex<Layer>> independently of pool ownership. New pending routes retain only the common leading outlier parent instances from the latest route (pending if present), configure those retained parents with latest settings, and allocate fresh deeper layers/leaf controller after the first kind difference. Counters/ejection multipliers/timer-start state of surviving parents persist while current and pending children overlap; retired inner instances remain separate. Both controllers can observe shared parent state, but each due check locks the layer and advances its deadline before another controller can execute that interval. Membership/counter access and pick masks now lock shared layers; no policy-owner back-reference is stored.

On successful route promotion the previous RR/weighted/outlier membership controller is explicitly aborted and releases weights/OOB registrations/outlier layer references, even if an old service reservation temporarily retains its Pool owner. PickFirst controller is likewise retired explicitly. Exact already-granted/dispatched Entry reservations and captured counter callbacks retain their independent lifetime; this source reasoning is not a measured cancellation/FIN/task-drain receipt. Pending supersession already drops its owned futures/pool and latest-source subscription. Shared physical singleton cache is retained through the existing cache boundary.

## Outlier wrapper entry retention across DNS replacement (2026-10-19)

Continues48b62ec5. Previously picker health and counters found Layer.entries by current SocketAddr. A shared parent map update from a pending nested child could remove/re-add an address while the old current child still served that address, causing old wrapper health/counters to read a different entry or lose its ejection. Native pool State now stores per-member outlier Binding objects created from the current map at wrapper/membership construction. Binding strongly retains the original Stats entry and weakly references its Layer; it does not retain a controller or policy-owner cycle.

Pool READY selection, membership health projection, weighted READY rebuild and dispatch counter capture all read those bindings. Removing an address stops its entry from future interval checks through the existing Layer.membership deletion, while old wrappers/calls keep that removed entry, including its last ejection state. Re-adding creates new Stats for new wrappers; old health/counters cannot alias the new entry. Same-member entries retained in the layer map preserve their Stats across membership rebuild. Explicit controller retirement now clears wrapper bindings with weights/layer references; already selected call counters remain independent. Count-enabled lookup is still latest Layer configuration at selection, with picker-publication snapshot fidelity retained as a separate gate.

## Outlier picker count-enabled publication snapshots (2026-10-19)

Continues bbda2fc4. Binding now stores a count-enabled boolean captured at native picker publication; Call.new reads this snapshot and retains the original Stats counter, rather than upgrading Layer and reading latest configuration at every pick. Configuration changes do not retroactively change an already selected call counter. Layer/controller weak ownership and removed-entry retention remain.

The membership controller now identifies picker publication on initial/membership application, observed Connectivity change (including ejection health/generation/failure), or weighted refresh. A plain outlier interval with no child-state change no longer publishes a replacement picker, and a weighted picker is not rebuilt merely because a separate outlier timer woke the task. Membership applied-ticket publication remains independent so pending decisions can complete.

Reference updateAddressList invokes child.updateAddressList before assigning latestConfig. Policy therefore captures previous parent counting flags before configuring shared parents; new outlier instances use false as their initial previous flag. Same-kind pool update similarly stages each previous layer flag. Bindings and the first applied-membership READY publication use those flags; an initial Connecting-only membership consumes the staged flags without producing a READY picker, so later READY publication reads latest settings. Non-membership weight/connectivity publications read current flags and do not prematurely consume a pending membership snapshot. This models the pre-latestConfig callback phase at the native publication boundary; full synchronous JS callback sequencing/coalesced observer equivalence remains unverified.

## Numeric grpc-status compatibility at native transport boundary (2026-10-19)

Continues6393e217. Reviewed pinned subchannel-call.ts handleTrailers Number(metadataMap[grpc-status]) and load-balancing-call.ts outputStatus listener/onCallEnded ordering. The native pool previously counted only literal grpc-status text0 as outlier success while Tonic also parsed raw status bytes directly. New grpc_lb_status.rs normalizes first-header values whose numeric conversion is a finite integer0..16 into canonical status text, before both outlier observer and Tonic see initial/trailers-only headers or final body trailers. Application and outlier now share the same supported status conversion boundary; signed/zero-padded/decimal/exponent values, unsigned0x/0o/0b literals, empty/ECMAScript whitespace-only values, negative zero and leading-zero integer strings can canonicalize. UTF8/grammar failures, fractions, nonfinite and out-of-range values remain untouched for existing Tonic handling, rather than inventing an enum code. No claim that this represents arbitrary JavaScript NaN/Infinity/fractional/out-of-enum status codes.

Status normalization changes only reserved grpc-status in the selected response; Entry/body retention, ORCA metrics fields and first-terminal counter guard remain. Missing status and transport/cancellation failures still count as failure on observer Drop. This does not establish complete logical/transport terminal accounting, HTTP fallback, decoder/cardinality/cancellation race parity, nor coverage for Buffered proxy/socket routes that bypass the pool.

Official docs consulted before implementation: gRPC HTTP2 response/trailer/status grammar https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md and ECMAScript StringToNumber/StringNumericLiteral https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tonumber-applied-to-the-string-type. The gRPC wire grammar is digit-only; broader Number syntax here preserves the pinned grpc-js1.14.4 receive behavior, not a request to generate noncanonical server statuses. Existing Tonic status boundary and pinned local source retained; Postman api-engineer workflow reused, no workspace/provider operation.

## Shared outlier health and deadline notifications (2026-10-19)

Continues d8cc5c2e. Shared Layer now owns a watch version for configuration/health/deadline changes. Every existing current/pending membership controller subscribes to its surviving parent layers, consumes versions before observing state, and awaits cloned receivers alongside member connectivity. Configuration/disable/uneject and completed interval checks notify all subscribers, so another controller that performed the shared check or shortened its timer cannot leave peers asleep until an obsolete local deadline. Tick advances the shared due time under the existing Layer mutex before notifying; a peer wake does not repeat the same interval. No extra worker/polling loop was introduced.

A watch change between observation and selecting on cloned receivers stays pending; constructor state is observed in the initial loop. Per-path parent layer identities are fixed for that pool, with a separate controller on path replacement. Existing picker-publication comparison suppresses new pickers for unchanged aggregate health, including intervals that only re-arm deadlines. Native health projection now marks an ejected member TF only when the physical singleton is READY; a never-selected Connecting child remains Connecting, matching pinned PickFirst currentPick-only health gating. Sticky post-TF leaf behavior and removed-entry Binding identity remain.

## ORCA compressed streams and tolerant binary reports (2026-10-19)

Continues9a64b38a. OOB OpenRcaService client now enables existing Tonic gzip/deflate receive support, as the normal native RPC/reflection client already does. Previously compressed ORCA reports could produce an unsupported-compression status and feed the producer UNIMPLEMENTED suppression path despite the service existing. Per-call endpoint-load-metrics-bin decoding now follows the tolerant ASCII Buffer boundary before Prost validation: accepts mixed standard/URL-safe alphabet and padding/no-padding, skips non-alphabet bytes/whitespace, stops at first equals, discards a dangling sextet, and permits unused trailing bits. Invalid protobuf is still ignored; no claim that this establishes reference malformed-protobuf exception behavior, repeated-header grouping or non-ASCII string coercion parity.

## Process-wide native DNS subchannel registry (2026-10-19)

Continuesc371e0af. SubchannelCache factories now enter a process-wide registry keyed by raw channel target, immutable Endpoint origin and effective connect timeout. Plaintext factories with matching scope share cached singleton owners across logical DNS routes. Existing grpc_transport::channel fixes user agent/other Endpoint settings; any new varying factory setting must be added to scope. RPC metadata/deadline and policy-local counters/weights are not copied into the physical connection scope. Buffered proxy/numeric/socket topology remains separate; this is not full cross-route/global-channel parity. Exact raw-target versus pinned canonical URI alias equality remains a fidelity gate.

Pinned subchannel-pool.ts compares target/address/channelOptions and ChannelCredentials._equals. channel-credentials.ts createSsl builds a new secureContext and _equals compares context/checkServerIdentity by reference, not certificate bytes. Current native channel() likewise constructs a fresh TLS config per invocation, so TLS registry scopes receive a fresh opaque UUID; cloning a cache retains that context scope, and new contexts/CA/client identities/verifiers cannot alias by PEM similarity. No credentials/material hashes are placed in registry keys or logs.

Registry holds cache owners through the existing10s unused-subchannel check rather than dropping them with the last logical handle. Empty owners are pruned only when registry plus the current cleanup/drop reference remain, checked under registry lock; concurrent factory lookup clones under that lock so an owner cannot disappear between lookup and get_or_create. Nested lock order is registry then cache, with cleanup releasing cache lock before pruning. Cleanup still captures Weak owner, stops on empty cache and restarts on use; empty never-used factories prune on Drop. Terminated singleton drivers are excluded/replaced on lookup, and a terminated cleanup task is restarted on use. Runtime-shutdown purge/concurrent-runtime behavior is not established.

## OOB watcher replacement and callback entry identity (2026-10-19)

Continuesf74b4211 retained weighted leaf updates. Applied membership now constructs a new OOB Registration before replacing/dropping the old one, matching PF create/ref-new-wrapper before unref-old-pick. Even unchanged report intervals notify the producer, including when an old call failed and backoff is pending. At least one watcher remains during replacement, preserving shared producer support/backoff state; disabling/removing the final watcher still destroys the producer. Ordinary weight/connectivity timer observations do not recreate registrations.

OOB Sink now binds the original EndpointWeight scalar entry, as the pinned oobMetricsListener closure captures entry. Late OOB data cannot update a freshly re-added same-address entry through current-map lookup. Per-request metric callbacks deliberately retain their current-map lookup behavior. The bound scalar contains no policy/leaf/IO owner, while config remains a shared latest-settings value; no controller retention cycle is added. Worker now tracks sampled watcher version and connectivity snapshot separately from borrow_and_update, so an update arriving while a different select branch wins cannot be consumed without authorizing a subscription attempt. All callbacks are still latest-state observers, not a proven full JS event ordering reconstruction.

## Initial DNS failure logical ownership (2026-10-19)

Initial DNS failure now returns an owned Dynamic route with an Unavailable picker rather than discarding the logical channel. Its resolver worker retries using the existing cached backoff until a successful lookup, with target-retirement cancellation and Owner drop aborts. The policy worker waits for accepted nonempty addresses and creates the desired child policy even when its signature matches the initial default. Successful initial lookups do not enter the bootstrap retry loop. ## Legacy deflate response configuration lists — 2026-10-19

Parent49b4cc23: pinned ws8.21.3 websocket.js checks unique extension names, not number of same-name configurations; permessage-deflate.js normalizes all configurations then acceptAsClient selects response[0]. Source parentd83ba084. Generate Code now routes the existing Python/http.client (python/python3) target to pythonHttpClientCode rather than the generic binary/custom-MIME refusal. ## Deleted collection cookie ownership: confirmed implementation gap — 2026-10-20

Source a25c6782 audit (no mutation). workspace.remove requests Stop without awaiting it, removes the collection/resources and queues persistence. Native CookieState::start_jar_owned admits a syntactically valid collection ID and caches Arc<PersistentJar>; PersistentJar::start_flush later writes that path, independent of saved collection membership. CookieProvider's generation check protects clear/edit snapshots but no collection-retirement generation exists. Therefore unlinking a cookie file only from the Delete UI can be undone by an already accepted flush and does not establish same-ID recreation isolation.

The required publication boundary has two current entry points: storage::write_workspace_file (ordinary Save and Git journal/Clone-install publication) and storage::restore_backup (reviewed raw backup replacement), both already wrap response_download::with_workspace_write. A cookie lifecycle implementation must cover both, maintain Git→Storage ordering and establish an explicit cookie-registry/jar lock order without acquiring Storage from a jar lock. It must fence old providers/queued flushes and new jar admission, bind retirement to a durably successful workspace publication, and recover an interrupted publication/cleanup from before/after identity rather than deleting arbitrary orphan files. Failed Save must preserve the previous active jar; restored/recreated same IDs must not silently revive a retired native jar. Active template-source cookie_jar resources retain their existing resource/import policy and are not blanket-replayed.

Next implementation work is this shared native publication/admission barrier and durable recovery, followed by reuse of the existing collection/cookie scenario where directly applicable. Do not add a UI-only unlink or a parallel native registry to make one Delete check pass. No cleanup, cookie/profile/native operation, source/testcase/helper/scenario change, new matrix, compiler/build rerun or live handles occurred during this audit. Existing CRUD/cookie/close/compiler receipts do not cover collection retirement. All original migration requirements remain open; this audit narrows the implementation entry points without waiving acceptance.
